subject: Nanotechnology
title: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells.

hook.text: A sponge of TiO₂ nanoparticles coated in dye absorbs light like a leaf — the Grätzel cell mimics photosynthesis.

buildup.text: Dye molecules inject excited electrons into the nano-TiO₂ scaffold — the porous structure provides enormous surface area.

discovery.text: DSSCs work in diffuse light and at wide angles — outperforming silicon indoors and on cloudy days.

twist.text: Liquid electrolyte can leak and evaporate — solid-state alternatives exist but reduce efficiency.

climax.text: Indoor DSSC panels now power IoT sensors in offices — harvesting ambient light that silicon cells ignore.

punchline.text: A nano sponge soaked in dye turns indoor light into power.

quiz.question: Why do dye-sensitized solar cells outperform silicon indoors?
options: Their dye molecules absorb diffuse light efficiently at wide angles
